column1: Answers to the problem of excessive electricity use by skyscrapers and large public buildings can be found in ingenious but forgotten architectural designs of the 19th and early-20th centuries
column2: 摩天大楼和大型公共建筑耗电过多，解决办法或许就藏在19世纪至20世纪初那些构思精巧、却已被遗忘的建筑设计里。
column5: large public buildings|大型公共建筑

column1: The Recovery of Natural Environments in Architecture by Professor Alan Short is the culmination of 30 years of research and award-winning green building design by Short and colleagues in Architecture, Engineering, Applied Maths and Earth Sciences at the University of Cambridge.
column2: 艾伦·肖特教授写了一本《在建筑中恢复自然环境》。这本书汇集了肖特与同事们30年来的研究成果和获奖绿色建筑设计。参与者来自剑桥大学的建筑、工程、应用数学和地球科学等领域。
column8: green building design|绿色建筑设计

column1: ‘The crisis in building design is already here,’ said Short.
column2: “建筑设计的危机已经来了。”肖特说。

column1: ‘Policy makers think you can solve energy and building problems with gadgets.
column2: “政策制定者以为，靠些新式设备就能解决能源和建筑问题。

column1: You can’t.
column2: 其实办不到。

column1: As global temperatures continue to rise, we are going to continue to squander more and more energy on keeping our buildings mechanically cool until we have run out of capacity.’
column2: 随着全球气温不断上升，我们将继续浪费越来越多的能源，用机械设备给建筑降温，直到再也无力维持下去。”
column7: run out of capacity|再也无力维持

column1: Short is calling for a sweeping reinvention of how skyscrapers and major public buildings are designed — to end the reliance on sealed buildings which exist solely via the ‘life support’ system of vast air conditioning units.
column2: 肖特呼吁彻底革新摩天大楼和大型公共建筑的设计方式，结束对密闭式建筑的依赖。这些建筑全靠庞大的空调机组充当“生命支持系统”才能维持运转。
column5: major public buildings|大型公共建筑

column1: Instead, he shows it is entirely possible to accommodate natural ventilation and cooling in large buildings by looking into the past, before the widespread introduction of air conditioning systems, which were ‘relentlessly and aggressively marketed’ by their inventors.
column2: 肖特指出，只要回望过去，就会发现大型建筑完全可以采用自然通风和降温的设计。那是空调系统还没有普及的年代，后来它的发明者才开始“不遗余力地大举推销”。

column1: Short points out that to make most contemporary buildings habitable, they have to be sealed and air conditioned.
column2: 肖特指出，如今大多数建筑要让人待得住，就必须密闭起来并装上空调。

column1: The energy use and carbon emissions this generates is spectacular and largely unnecessary.
column2: 这种做法所消耗的能源和产生的碳排放量都大得惊人，而且大多没有必要。

column1: Buildings in the West account for 40-50% of electricity usage, generating substantial carbon emissions, and the rest of the world is catching up at a frightening rate.
column2: 在西方，建筑用电占总用电量的40%至50%，产生了大量碳排放。世界其他地区也正以令人担忧的速度赶上来。
column8: at a frightening rate|以令人担忧的速度

column1: Short regards glass, steel and air-conditioned skyscrapers as symbols of status, rather than practical ways of meeting our requirements.
column2: 在肖特看来，用玻璃和钢材建造、靠空调调温的摩天大楼象征着地位，却不是满足实际需要的可行方式。
column8: meeting our requirements|满足我们的需要

column1: Short’s book highlights a developing and sophisticated art and science of ventilating buildings through the 19th and earlier-20th centuries, including the design of ingeniously ventilated hospitals.
column2: 肖特的书展示了19世纪至20世纪早期日渐成熟的建筑通风艺术与科学，其中包括一些通风构思精巧的医院设计。
column7: ventilated hospitals|设有通风系统的医院

column1: Of particular interest were those built to the designs of John Shaw Billings, including the first Johns Hopkins Hospital in the US city of Baltimore (1873-1889).
column2: 尤其引人关注的是按约翰·肖·比林斯的图纸建成的医院，其中包括美国巴尔的摩市最初的约翰斯·霍普金斯医院（1873—1889年）。
column3: Of particular interest|尤为引人关注
column4: built to the designs of|按照……的设计建造
column6: Johns Hopkins Hospital|约翰斯·霍普金斯医院

column1: ‘We spent three years digitally modelling Billings’ final designs,’ says Short.
column2: 肖特说：“我们用了三年，为比林斯最后定稿的设计建立数字模型。

column1: ‘We put pathogens* in the airstreams, modelled for someone with tuberculosis (TB) coughing in the wards and we found the ventilation systems in the room would have kept other patients safe from harm.’
column2: 我们在模型的气流中加入病原体，模拟有结核病患者在病房里咳嗽的情形，结果发现，房间里的通风系统本可以保护其他患者免受感染。”

column1: ‘We discovered that 19th-century hospital wards could generate up to 24 air changes an hour — that’s similar to the performance of a modern-day, computer-controlled operating theatre.
column2: “我们发现，19世纪的医院病房每小时换气可达24次，这与如今电脑控制的手术室表现相当。

column1: We believe you could build wards based on these principles now.
column2: 我们相信，现在也能依据这些原理建造病房。

column1: Single rooms are not appropriate for all patients.
column2: 单人病房并非适合所有患者。

column1: Communal wards appropriate for certain patients — older people with dementia, for example — would work just as well in today’s hospitals, at a fraction of the energy cost.’
column2: 对某些患者，如患有失智症的老年人，多人病房是合适的选择。在今天的医院里，这种病房同样管用，能源开支却只需一小部分。”
column9: at a fraction of|只需……的一小部分

column1: Professor Short contends the mindset and skill-sets behind these designs have been completely lost, lamenting the disappearance of expertly designed theatres, opera houses, and other buildings where up to half the volume of the building was given over to ensuring everyone got fresh air.
column2: 肖特教授认为，当年支撑这些设计的思维方式和整套本领，如今已完全失传。他惋惜那些设计精良的剧院、歌剧院和其他建筑已经消失。在那些建筑里，多达一半的建筑容积曾用于确保每个人都能呼吸到新鲜空气。

column1: Much of the ingenuity present in 19th-century hospital and building design was driven by a panicked public clamouring for buildings that could protect against what was thought to be the lethal threat of miasmas — toxic air that spread disease.
column2: 19世纪医院和其他建筑中的许多巧思，是在公众的恐慌情绪推动下产生的。人们强烈要求建筑能够抵御当时被视为致命威胁的“瘴气”，也就是会传播疾病的毒气。

column1: Miasmas were feared as the principal agents of disease and epidemics for centuries, and were used to explain the spread of infection from the Middle Ages right through to the cholera outbreaks in London and Paris during the 1850s.
column2: 几百年来，人们都畏惧瘴气，将其视为疾病与疫病流行的主要根源。从中世纪一直到19世纪50年代伦敦和巴黎暴发霍乱，感染的蔓延一直被归咎于瘴气。

column1: Foul air, rather than germs, was believed to be the main driver of ‘hospital fever’, leading to disease and frequent death.
column2: 当时人们认为，污浊的空气才是导致“医院热”的主因，而非病菌；由此不少人患病，死亡也屡见不鲜。

column1: The prosperous steered clear of hospitals.
column2: 有钱人都尽量避开医院。

column1: While miasma theory has been long since disproved, Short has for the last 30 years advocated a return to some of the building design principles produced in its wake.
column2: 尽管瘴气说早已被证伪，过去30年来，肖特一直主张重新采用一些在这种理论影响下形成的建筑设计原则。

column1: Today, huge amounts of a building’s space and construction cost are given over to air conditioning.
column2: 如今，建筑中大量的空间和相当大的一部分建造费用，都花在了空调上。

column1: ‘But I have designed and built a series of buildings over the past three decades which have tried to reinvent some of these ideas and then measure what happens.’
column2: “不过，过去30年里，我设计并建造了一系列建筑，试着用新的方式实践其中一些旧构想，再实际测量其效果。”

column1: ‘To go forward into our new low-energy, low-carbon future, we would be well advised to look back at design before our high-energy, high-carbon present appeared.
column2: “要走向新的低能耗、低碳未来，我们最好回过头去看看，在今天这种高能耗、高碳局面出现之前，人们是怎样设计建筑的。

column1: What is surprising is what a rich legacy we have abandoned.’
column2: 令人吃惊的是，我们竟舍弃了如此丰厚的遗产。”

column1: Successful examples of Short’s approach include the Queen’s Building at De Montfort University in Leicester.
column2: 肖特的设计理念已有成功案例，莱斯特德蒙福特大学的女王楼就是一例。
column7: De Montfort University|德蒙福特大学

column1: Containing as many as 2,000 staff and students, the entire building is naturally ventilated, passively cooled and naturally lit, including the two largest auditoria, each seating more than 150 people.
column2: 这栋楼能容纳多达2000名师生，整栋建筑都采用自然通风、被动式降温和自然采光，其中也包括最大的两间报告厅，每间都能容纳150多人就座。
column4: staff and students|教职工和学生

column1: The award-winning building uses a fraction of the electricity of comparable buildings in the UK.
column2: 这栋获奖建筑的用电量，只相当于英国同类建筑的一小部分。
column6: comparable buildings|可作比较的同类建筑

column1: Short contends that glass skyscrapers in London and around the world will become a liability over the next 20 or 30 years if climate modelling predictions and energy price rises come to pass as expected.
column2: 肖特认为，未来二三十年，伦敦乃至世界各地的玻璃摩天大楼都将成为一种负担，前提是气候模型的预测应验，能源价格也如预期那样上涨。
column8: energy price rises|能源价格上涨

column1: He is convinced that sufficiently cooled skyscrapers using the natural environment can be produced in almost any climate.
column2: 他确信，在几乎任何一种气候条件下，都能建成借助自然环境充分降温的摩天大楼。
column6: almost any climate|几乎任何气候条件

column1: He and his team have worked on hybrid buildings in the harsh climates of Beijing and Chicago — built with natural ventilation assisted by back-up air conditioning — which, surprisingly perhaps, can be switched off more than half the time on milder days and during the spring and autumn.
column2: 他和团队曾在气候严酷的北京和芝加哥研究混合通风建筑：建筑采用自然通风，另有备用空调辅助。也许出人意料的是，在天气较温和的日子以及春秋两季，空调有一半以上的时间可以关闭。
column3: hybrid buildings|结合两种通风方式的建筑
column8: more than half the time|超过一半的时间
column9: milder days|气候较温和的日子

column1: Short looks at how we might reimagine the cities, offices and homes of the future.
column2: 肖特思考的是，我们可以怎样重新设想未来的城市、办公室和住宅。

column1: Maybe it’s time we changed our outlook.
column2: 也许，我们该换一种眼光了。
column5: outlook|n. 观念，看问题的方式
